title: 3rd sitting of the 20th Majlis
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla (opening and voting); Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim presided during the debate
summary: The Majlis opened its 3rd sitting, introduced a bill to amend the Immigration Act, and approved Ibrahim Shujau as its member of the Clemency Board. It also sent two presidential ambassador nominations to the Foreign Relations Committee. Most of the sitting was an hour-long debate on a Land Act amendment bill on allocating housing plots in Male' region, which the President had returned for reconsideration. A motion to refer it to committee failed, and the vote to pass it unchanged also failed, so the bill lapsed.

items.title: Attendance of members
items.outcome: 66 members present; none on leave or official travel

items.title: First reading of bill to amend the Immigration Act (Law 1/2007), sponsored by Meekail Ahmed Nasym
Chair's announcement on who presides over sittings; Speaker hands chair to Deputy Speaker
items.outcome: Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim took the chair while the Speaker left to attend the JSC oath

items.title: Appointing a Majlis member to the Clemency Board
items.outcome: Ibrahim Shujau (Baarashu) nominated and seconded; approved 88-0

items.title: President's letter nominating ambassadors to Turkey and Pakistan
items.outcome: Referred to the Foreign Relations Committee

items.title: Ninth amendment to the Land Act (Law 1/2002), returned by the President for reconsideration
items.outcome: Debated; referral to committee failed 12-75; passing unchanged failed 12-76; bill lapsed

items.title: Votes on matters ready for decision
items.outcome: Three votes held (Clemency Board, committee referral, bill unchanged)

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Nominated Ibrahim Shujau for the Clemency Board.
Said a three-month handover of plots in areas not yet reclaimed is unrealistic and criticised the previous government's housing record.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Seconded the Clemency Board nomination.
Said housing is a real concern but bills need thorough study, and the President's return of this bill raises genuine issues.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Moved to send the bill to the National Development and Heritage Committee to be amended.
Said the majority could write a workable handover timeline if it wanted to fix the problem.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Raised a point of order that a speaker had strayed from the topic.
Said the amendment was not made in good faith and he would not support taking it forward.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Said the bill should not proceed as drafted given the President's letter and a new land bill coming; supported returning it.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Said housing matters but passing the bill as drafted would not help residents; backed the President's letter and rejecting the bill.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Argued the bill should be dropped now, since the government is expected to send a fuller land bill, rather than spend time on it.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Called the issue sensitive and said Male' residents deserve a fair chance at plots; supported sending the bill back to committee.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said a legal three-month handover of plots in unreclaimed areas is impractical and questioned how earlier plots were allocated.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said the bill was not made in good faith, citing plots in unreclaimed areas and an unconfirmed housing minister.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Questioned whether earlier plot allocations followed the Land Act and supported rejecting the bill in favour of a fairer nationwide system.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Said the country needs a long-term housing policy and land-use plan, and asked that committee work keep this in view.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Said housing is a major national problem, criticised the previous government's record and backed the President's decision.

speakers.name: Hussain Imran Latheef
positions: Said President Muizzu has worked on Male' housing and that the bill should be sent back or reworked.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Said committee time should not be used on this bill because the government has prepared a fuller land bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Disputed earlier claims about Hulhumale' land and said plots can be allocated quickly; text is garbled in places.

decisions: Ibrahim Shujau (Baarashu) approved as the Majlis member of the Clemency Board, 88 yes, none against.
Presidential nominations of ambassadors to Turkey and Pakistan sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
Motion to refer the returned Land Act amendment bill to the National Development and Heritage Committee failed, 12 yes to 75 no.
Vote to pass the returned Land Act amendment bill unchanged failed, 12 yes to 76 no, so the bill lapsed.
Bill to amend the Immigration Act had its first reading.
Next sitting set for Monday 10 June 2024 at 9:00.

votes.what: Appoint Ibrahim Shujau to the Clemency Board
Refer the returned Land Act (9th amendment) bill to the National Development and Heritage Committee
Pass the returned Land Act (9th amendment) bill without changes
